name: apt
summary: Installs, updates and removes software (Debian, Ubuntu).
description: The package manager of Debian and Ubuntu. It downloads software from the repositories and handles its dependencies automatically. Operations that change the system require sudo. Two steps not to mix up: apt update refreshes the list of available versions, apt upgrade actually installs the updates.

options.description: Does not install packages that are merely recommended, only the required dependencies.
Shows what would be done, without changing anything.
With list, only packages that have an update.

subcommands.name: update
subcommands.description: Downloads the up-to-date list of available packages (installs nothing).

subcommands.name: upgrade
subcommands.description: Installs new versions of packages that are already installed.

subcommands.name: full-upgrade
subcommands.description: Like upgrade, but can also remove or add packages to resolve dependencies.

subcommands.name: install
subcommands.description: Installs one or more packages, with their dependencies.

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.description: Uninstalls a package while keeping its configuration files.

subcommands.name: purge
subcommands.description: Uninstalls a package and also deletes its configuration.

subcommands.name: autoremove
subcommands.description: Removes dependencies that were installed automatically and are no longer needed.

subcommands.name: search
subcommands.description: Searches for a package by keyword in names and descriptions.

subcommands.name: show
subcommands.description: Shows the details of a package: version, size, dependencies, description.

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.description: List of packages, to filter with --installed or --upgradable.

arguments.name: PACKAGE
arguments.description: Name(s) of the package(s) the subcommand acts on.

examples.command: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade
examples.explanation: The classic update: refresh the list, then install the new versions.
Installs git and curl without asking for confirmation.

examples.command: sudo apt purge apache2 && sudo apt autoremove
examples.explanation: Completely uninstalls Apache, then cleans up unneeded dependencies.
The packages that have an update available.

dangerNote: Read the list of packages to be removed before confirming: remove or full-upgrade can take away packages that other software depends on. -y skips this check.
